etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English standen, stonden (verb) and stand, stond (noun, from the verb), from Old English standan (“to stand, occupy a place”), from Proto-West Germanic *standan, from Proto-Germanic *standaną (“to stand”), from Pre-Germanic *sth₂-n-t-´, an innovative extended n-infixed form of Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, copulative) To support oneself on the feet in an erect position.

(intransitive, copulative) To remain motionless.

etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English stand, stande, stond, stonde, stoonde, probably from Middle Dutch stande, from Old Dutch *standan (“to stand”), from Frankish *standan.

Forms with -o- may show influence of stonden (“stand”, verb).

definitions.definition: (US, Scotland, dated) A container which stands upright, such as a barrel or cask.
